cards.title: Declutter the map: colleagues live in the coin tray; Owner view groups by owner
cards.detail:
Both Domain view and Owner view carry a full row of colleague furniture — colleague buildings, the campfire, and four locked bench seats — across the neutral middle of the map. That furniture predates the coin tray (RavenBench), which is now a fixed top bar on every tab (the Map tab included) and is already the agent action surface: a coin fires plays today. With the tray in place, the map no longer needs to host colleagues.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-13):
- Domain view loses the entire landmark row: colleague buildings, campfire, and locked seats.
- Owner view works exactly like Domain view (same work-geography — contexts, projects, systems, stray piles) except each region is labelled and grouped by its owner (e.g. 'DANVERS', from domain.owner with the human:/colleague: prefix stripped) instead of its domain name (e.g. 'SOFTWARE'). Ownership is not assumed 1:1 with domains: a domain may map to a single owner (then the two views differ only in the label), or ownership may regroup regions.
- The two features the colleague building overlay carried — the work journal and the Needs-a-Human lane — move onto the colleague's coin as coin actions.
- The colleague-level escalation cue moves with them: a coin glows or badges when its colleague has a Needs-a-Human item or an overdue/unhealthy system, preserving the at-a-glance signal the building glow used to give. Tile-level Needs-a-Human glow stays on the work tile (L1) unchanged.

Scope:
- Domain-view layout: stop rendering the colleague/seat/campfire landmark layer (MapLandmarks renders in both modes today; skip the whole row in Domain view).
- Owner view: reuse the Domain-view work layout; label and group regions by domain.owner rather than name; keep an owner-less region visibly unclaimed (demand signal, plan §1.2).
- Coin (RavenBench): add Journal and Needs-a-Human actions to the coin action menu; wire the coin lit/activated state to a colleague-level escalation rollup.

Out of scope:
- Placement UX for unplaced projects (tracked separately, in flight).
- The long-term question of whether the map becomes purely work and whether Owner view survives — noted in the Map Glow Up thread, not decided here.

Status: delivered — #32 (Domain-view declutter), #35 (coin Journal + Needs-a-Human actions + colleague-escalation glow), #36 (Owner view = domain layout labelled by owner). Colleagues now live entirely in the coin tray. Notes: Owner view is a read-only lens (no tile/pile click overlays); the escalation-glow data is scoped to map/info surfaces (v1, no new app-wide polling); e2e/visual verification pending CI restoration.

cards.title: Unify and de-cruft the Map and Work Board data models onto one taxonomy spine
cards.detail:
The Map (docs/alexandria/map/map-state.json) and the Work Board (docs/alexandria/info-hub/board-state.json) grew up separately and now describe the same work with three colliding vocabularies: the Map uses domain/context as work-geography, the Board uses a flat `area` (viewer/library/runtime/ops) that matches no Map context, and the library's knowledge-organization cards use domain/context/plane for card storage. 'Alexandria' is overloaded too — it names the whole org's knowledge system AND one product domain. Goal: one authoritative taxonomy spine both surfaces read, so a work item's home is the same word on the Board and on the Map.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-13):
- Organization = SocioTechnica. Give the org and the product domain distinct ids (org `sociotechnica`, domain `alexandria`) so one noun never means two levels.
- Domains are the Map's single organizing level and the shared join key across Map, Board, and library. New set: Alexandria (Raven), Skillmaker.Studio (William), New Media (Damien), Business Development (Rob). Supersedes the old Software/New Media pair and the library's stale Operations/Product/Sales & Marketing/Software Development.
- Planes and Contexts stay library-side (information organization). The Map organizes by Domain only; Planes never touch the Map. Context is deferred: keep it as an optional, nullable tag but do not render or organize by it yet — 'model it, don't render it.'
- Projects and Systems are flat tags placed on a Domain, not a nesting hierarchy. Stray work (no project, no system) is a first-class case.
- One spine, both surfaces: retire the Board's `area` field for the shared Domain id; systematize the optional contextId/entityId tags that already exist on some Board cards.

Scope:
- This is the parent. The concrete migrations are the child cards: reset the Map domain model, retire the Board `area` field, and stray-task placement v1.
- Write the taxonomy down once (org → domain → {project | system | stray}, context as a latent tag) as the shape both map-state.json and board-state.json conform to.

Out of scope (on the 'other things discussed' list, not here):
- Library updates for the pivot (Entity - Domain, colleague cards for William & Rob, rename Playmaker→Skillmaker, card the Board entities).
- Map 'filling up' visualization (piles/aging/stomp).
- Rebuilding plays to run Fabro-less.
- Subsume vs federate: is the Board a permanent peer surface or a way-station until the Map absorbs it? Named, not decided.

cards.title: Reset the Map's domain model to the post-pivot org
cards.detail:
map-state.json still carries the pre-pivot shape: two domains (Software owned by human:danvers, New Media owned by colleague:damien), contexts (Viewer, Colleagues, Demos) acting as containers, and entities nested inside a context by contextId. Bring it to the decided model. Child of wo-unify-map-board-data-model.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-13):
- Add the organization level `sociotechnica`, kept distinct from the `alexandria` domain id.
- Domains (the only Map organizing level): `alexandria`, `skillmaker-studio`, `new-media`, `business-development`. Retire `software`.
- Proposed owners follow the New-Media=Damien pattern — each domain owned by its colleague: alexandria→colleague:raven, skillmaker-studio→colleague:william, new-media→colleague:damien, business-development→colleague:rob. Confirm before applying (director-as-owner vs colleague-as-owner is a real choice).
- Projects and Systems become flat tags carrying `domainId` directly; they no longer nest inside a Context.
- Context stops being a container. Keep `contextId` as an optional, nullable tag for the future experiment, but nothing organizes or renders by it.
- Multi-domain entity placement: lands in the owner's domain, ideally rendered at the border with the other domain it touches. A System must have an owner.

Scope:
- map-state.json: introduce the org level; replace the domains array; assign owners and hex regions for the four domains; retag entities with domainId; relax the context-as-container assumption.
- Migrate existing entities (sys-raven-duty-loop, sys-damien-duty-loop, the three prj-* projects) onto the new domains without loss.

Out of scope:
- Board changes (wo-board-retire-area-field). Pile/stray visualization (wo-map-stray-tasks-and-placement-v1).

cards.title: Retire the Work Board's `area` field; tag work items by domain
cards.detail:
Every Board card carries an `area` (viewer / library / runtime / ops) that predates the Map and matches no Map domain or context — a parallel, ad-hoc taxonomy. Replace it with the shared spine so a card's home is the same word the Map uses. Child of wo-unify-map-board-data-model.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-13):
- Every work item carries a `domainId` from the shared domain set (its primary home).
- `contextId` and `entityId` stay optional (a card may point at a Map project/system, or be a stray with neither) — the same fields two Board cards already use; make them consistent rather than ad-hoc.
- Retire `area`. Today's values are all really Alexandria sub-areas: viewer/library/runtime/ops → domain `alexandria`. Any finer within-domain split is a Context concern, which stays latent for now.

Scope:
- board-state.json: add `domainId` to the card shape; migrate all existing cards (today's mapping: viewer/library/runtime/ops → alexandria; re-home any that are truly another domain); drop `area`.
- Keep contextId/entityId optional; leave stray cards with neither.
- Coordinate with the open card 'Wire GET/POST /api/info-hub/board' so the board validator learns domainId and forgets area.

Out of scope:
- Map-side changes (wo-map-reset-domain-model). Deciding the finer within-domain split (Context) — deferred.

cards.title: Stray tasks v1 + entity placement rules on the Map
cards.detail:
With Projects and Systems as flat Domain tags, a work item can have neither — a 'stray.' The director isn't yet confident how strays should behave and expects to iterate; this is a deliberately simple v1 to start, not the final answer. Child of wo-unify-map-board-data-model.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-13):
- Stray = a task with no project and no system.
- v1 placement: a stray piles in its owner's Domain. A stray with no domain at all piles in an 'unclaimed' zone, rendered visibly unclaimed as a demand signal (reuse the owner-less-region concept from wo-map-declutter-colleagues-to-tray).
- Multi-domain entity (a sprint-like Project or a shared System touching several domains): lands and displays in the owner's Domain, ideally at the border with the other domain it touches. A System must have an owner.

Scope:
- Data: represent a stray (project=null, system=null) with an optional domainId.
- Map render: a per-domain stray pile, plus an unclaimed pile for domain-less strays.
- Placement rule for multi-domain entities (owner's domain, border-preferred).

Explicitly experimental:
- Expect this to change with real use. The bigger visualization question — piles vs vertical stacks, how work shows aging/problematic, whether you stomp a pile to clear it — is tracked separately, governed by the command-center test (act on the pile where you see it).

cards.title: Adopt the work-system contract: the Board is the system of record; the Map visualizes it
cards.detail:
The Map and the Board now share one domain vocabulary, but the relationship between them was never ruled. Ruled today. This is the parent card; the concrete builds are the child cards joined to prj-work-system-v1.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-14):
- The Work Board is the work system of record and the QA surface — a known, simple, non-innovative primitive to generate the Map from. The Map is a reflection of the work system. This settles the open subsume-vs-federate question for now: federate. Deeper unification (less UI surface between board and map, or the map absorbing the board) stays a horizon option, not a plan.
- Systems generate work; projects contain it. This ratifies the ported Lifebuild 'Planting Season' contract (docs/alexandria/plans/map-tab/plan.md §1.1) as the unified model: a System spawns cards on its rhythm (e.g. 'check and respond to customer emails' every 6 hours); a Project is stuffed with cards, still exists when half are done, and its membership changes over time (tasks removed, tasks added).
- Every map entity gets a room: clicking a Project or System shows that entity's own populated view — its cards, their state, their history. The room already exists (the Map tile-click overlay renders joined cards via cardsJoinedToEntity), but it is starved: only 6 of 14 cards carry an entityId and both systems have zero.
- Projects and Systems measure different things, so their rooms differ. Project room = progress: contains work, ends, victories stay visible. System room = health & performance: is work done on time and to spec, is the system reliable and maintained, what is queued for testing or improving it.

Scope:
- This is the parent/contract card. Children: ungate the entity join (wo-board-ungate-entity-join), create-from-board + rooms on the board (wo-board-project-rooms), system generation v1 (wo-system-generation-v1).

Out of scope:
- Subsume (the Map absorbing the Board) — named horizon, not decided.
- A single unified Project/System/Task work-item model with real parent/child ('one day we may be more unified').
- The map filling-up visualization experiments (piles/aging/stomp) — still governed by the command-center test.

cards.title: Drop the Context picker; ungate the project/system join on the Board
cards.detail:
The New Work Order form still shows 'map Context (optional)' and gates the project picker behind it — the form filters entities to entity.contextId === selectedContext, so with Context deprecated a card can't reach a project at all. This is why the director cannot assign a task to a project today. Child of wo-work-system-contract.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-14):
- Remove the Context picker from the work-order form; Context stays a latent data field only ('model it, don't render it' still stands).
- Ungate the entity picker: a card can join any Project or System directly (optionally narrowed by the card's domainId, never by context).
- Finish the context demotion in the map data model: packages/ax/src/effects/map-state.ts still requires contextId as a mandatory string referencing a known context on every entity, despite the demotion ruling — make it optional/nullable there and in the entity form.
- Join the backlog: sweep the existing cards and join the ones that clearly belong to an entity (e.g. duty-loop-shaped cards to their systems), so the rooms stop rendering empty.

Scope:
- Work-order form: remove the Context field; entity picker lists all projects and systems.
- map-state.ts + MapEntityForm: contextId optional/nullable.
- board-state.json: backlog join pass (data only, no shape change).

Out of scope:
- Creating entities from the Board and the board-side room view (wo-board-project-rooms).

Status: delivered — Context picker removed, entity picker ungated, contextId optional end-to-end (ax validator, viewer schema, entity form), placement re-keyed off domainId. Backlog join sweep: no additional clear joins found — remaining unjoined cards are genuine strays (no matching entity exists for them).

cards.title: Create projects from the Board; give every entity a room on the Board
cards.detail:
Today a Project or System can only be born by hand in map-state.json or via the Map's entity form, and the only per-entity view is the Map tile-click overlay. The Board — the system of record — can neither create an entity nor show one. This blocks 'create a project and build it out of tasks.' Child of wo-work-system-contract.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-14):
- 'New project' (and 'New system') actions on the Board create the map entity directly. The entity is born unplaced; placement stays director-only on the Map (the ported hard rule: agents and forms may add entities, only the director arranges the map).
- Every entity gets a room reachable from the Board: the entity's cards, their state, and their history — the same entityId join the Map overlay already computes (cardsJoinedToEntity in packages/viewer/src/components/map/placement.ts). Done cards stay visible in the room: a project outlives its tasks, and its history is part of the room.
- The project room reads as progress (open vs done, the contained set changing over time). The system room will diverge toward health/performance — designed in wo-system-generation-v1, not here.

Scope:
- Board UI: New project / New system actions writing through the existing map-state save path.
- Board UI: an entity room view (entity header + joined cards, open and done), shared-component with the Map overlay rather than duplicated.
- Unplaced entities: confirm the Map renders/queues them sanely until the director places them.

Out of scope:
- Cadence generation and system health metrics (wo-system-generation-v1).
- Any change to what the Map overlay shows (it already works; reuse, don't fork).

Status: delivered — shared EntityRoomBody extracted from the Map overlay (overlay unchanged); Board gains an entity strip, per-entity rooms with ?entity= deep links, and New project / New system actions creating unplaced entities through the existing map save path; rooms show open and done cards with the completed-project read-only rule.

cards.title: Systems generate their work: pattern-spawned cards + a health-first system room
cards.detail:
RESCOPED (director, 2026-07-14): the single-cadence v1 is superseded by the full work-systems model — plural pattern rules, real controls (on-time %, streak, next due), multi-level ownership (system owner / upgrade-project owner / per-rule task assignee), and the upgrade-project loop. Plan: docs/alexandria/plans/work-system/plan.md (issues WS1-WS6 become this card's children). Source: docs/alexandria/sources/2026-07-14-work-systems-and-map-first-inversion.md.

Original scope (kept for history): The contract says a System generates cards, but nothing generates today — both systems have zero joined cards, and system health derives only from duty-loop journal entries within the cadence window (plan §1.4). Lifebuild had recurring-task machinery (recurringTasks/taskExecutions) and the port deliberately left it behind as legacy AI-cron; this rebuilds the behavior natively on the Board, where the work system of record lives. Child of wo-work-system-contract.

Decisions (director, 2026-07-14):
- A System spawns a card on its cadence (e.g. 'check and respond to customer emails' every 6 hours), joined to the system via entityId, assigned to the system's assignee.
- Spawned cards done or missed become the system's history, and the system room reads health and performance from it: done on time? to spec? what's the queue for testing or improving the system?
- Flagged experimental like strays v1 — the director expects to iterate; ship something simple to start.

Open design (decide in-card, small):
- Who spawns: the colleague duty loop writing cards as part of its rhythm, an ax runtime tick, or materialize-on-read when the board is loaded past a cadence boundary. v1 should pick the simplest that leaves a durable file trace (no server-owned state).
- Missed-cadence semantics: does an unspawned/undone card mark the system overdue, and does that feed the existing coin/tile escalation glow?

Scope:
- Card shape: a way to mark a card as system-generated (e.g. source: system:<id>) so history queries are cheap.
- Generation v1 for the two duty-loop systems as the first real users.
- System room v1: health summary (on-time rate over the recent window) + open queue + history, distinct from the project room's progress framing.

Out of scope:
- General recurring-task UI for arbitrary schedules; template libraries.
- Reviving Lifebuild's recurringTasks/taskExecutions machinery as-is.
